J2.evidence: In the verse «وكان أكلا قاعدا وشخا ... تحت رواق البيت يغشى الدخا», the word «شخّ» (to urinate) is in the Arabic, so '[abdest bozmak]' is strictly the rendering of an existing word, not new content. But the Turkish puts it in bare square brackets (no Mütercim notu), which tells the reader it is a translator insertion and leaves «وشخا» looking untranslated; it also softens 'urinate' to the general 'relieve oneself'. The reading still needs a fix: render وشخا plainly in the running text (e.g. 'oturup yiyip ... işediği'), without brackets. The rest of the lugha, i'rab and fawa'id was checked and is faithful.

J1.evidence: In the poem «وكان أكلا قاعدا وشخا ... تحت رواق البيت يغشى الدخا» the Turkish has 'dumana bürünüp [abdest bozmak] işi olduğunda'. The bracketed '[abdest bozmak]' is an unmarked addition, not a «Mütercim notu». It also does not properly render وشخا (he urinated) as part of the line. The English renders it plainly as 'passing water'. Fix: translate شخا in the text, or put the gloss inside «[Mütercim notu: …]».
